statement: For a runtime service carrying fresh non-empty data-affinity weights, the suboptimality observer and the placement intent share one decision: whenever isDataAffinityPlacementSuboptimal reports true, the same evaluation evidence yields a minted REPLACE toward an affinity-preferred feasible node through the existing full-score placement intent — or the observer does not report true — so detection can never latch without a cure. Modeled on the exact 2026-07-21T15:06:54 live ordering (svc-movielens-topn healthy 2 of desired 2 across 5 nodes, observer fired once on the affinity term, rebalance() ran and minted zero moves, weightedLocality stayed 0.000 for 300s with attributionRows=2 and working top-10), proven by a deterministic discriminator at the observer-intent seam that is red on current HEAD, with no new scoring formula (only the existing kernel terms and margins), no churn below the incumbent-retention margin, no flag or disable switch, byte-identical behavior for entities without preferDataAffinity, and the unchanged five-node MovieLens live scenario converging weightedLocality above zero once planning is admitted.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Data affinity remains intrinsic policy: no feature flag, disable switch, or per-call option may be introduced, and no flag may survive the session. Entities without preferDataAffinity retain byte-identical behavior.

Reuse only the existing placement-kernel terms and margins (NODE_AFFINITY_WEIGHT, group weights, INCUMBENT_MOVEMENT_COST retention margin). The fix aligns the observer and the intent on the same inequality and candidate universe; it must not introduce a second scorer, new weights, or new constants beyond naming existing scalars.

No REPLACE may be planned when the affinity gradient does not exceed the existing incumbent-retention movement margin. The parity fix must not increase move churn for states the full-score intent already ranks as keep-incumbent correctly.

The MovePlanner placement kernel remains the single owner of the move decision. The observer must not mint moves, mutate state, or re-derive placement outside the kernel; parity is achieved by sharing the kernel's own decision surface, not by duplicating it.

Before source change acceptance, a deterministic discriminator at the real observer-intent seam must reproduce the 2026-07-21T15:06:54 detect-without-cure state (fresh non-empty affinity weights favoring data nodes, incumbents holding none of the accessed data, observer true, zero minted moves), stay red on current HEAD, be red-on-revert for any fix, and include negative controls proving no move is minted below the retention margin and no behavior change for entities without preferDataAffinity.
